editorial.headline: Farm-Tool Retail: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Agricultural-tool retail is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks its registration there.
editorial.body:
Retail trade in agricultural tools may sound narrow until the shop floor comes into view. This activity covers the retail sale of farm implements: hoes, ploughs, sickles, crowbars and non-mechanical rice threshers. The record also places it alongside direct selling. The category is defined by the sale of those practical agricultural tools, not by a broad label alone; its examples give the description its useful boundaries.

That specificity matters when the activity is stated in a company’s registration. The named goods range from digging and cutting implements to crowbars and a rice-threshing tool that is explicitly non-mechanical, giving the retail offer a distinctly agricultural-tool focus. It is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. The slim record supplies no further operating prescription, so the sound reading is a disciplined one: keep the description anchored to the listed retail goods and to direct selling, rather than adding conditions it does not state.

Nationally, the investment posture is clear. The activity is TERBUKA for PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. A foreign investor can therefore hold the full national foreign-ownership ceiling for this activity in a PMA registration. The national basis cited in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That clarity is substantial, yet it is not the end of the analysis for a business intended to register in Bali.

Bali changes the conclusion decisively. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk assessment is Low/Medium-Low across every scope, and the record identifies this as the trigger for Bali’s moratorium in May 2026. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. A national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling does not turn into a Bali registration route when that moratorium applies. For founders, the honest answer is simple: national openness exists on the record, while Bali is blocked for PMA registration.
